name: MT deferred sell burn drains the MT/WBNB pair on a permissionless trigger
summary: During MT's deflation phase each sell adds its net amount to pendingBurnAmount, and the next extractFromPoolForLpMining, run by the LP-mining contract 0x139bd2ec whose distributeDailyRewards anyone can call once a day, burns that amount straight out of the MT/WBNB pair 0x037e6eb2 (down to a 21,000 MT floor) and syncs. Buys are banned in that phase, but transfers between two fee-excluded addresses skip every check, and the owner had excluded both the pair and the PancakeSwap router. With 358,681 WBNB flash-borrowed from Moolah, the attack contract minted a dust LP position from 0.2 MT (the referral-binding amount, also exempt), bought 10M MT twice with the router as recipient (496.66 and 717.55 WBNB) and pulled them out with removeLiquidityETHSupportingFeeOnTransferTokens, sold 10M MT inside a flash-swap callback (397.33 WBNB out, pendingBurnAmount +9M), called distributeDailyRewards to burn 6,735,517 MT from the pair, leaving 21,000 MT against about 1,201 WBNB, and sold 10M MT for 1,198.63 WBNB, netting 381.75 WBNB.
notes: Reset is the owner's setLpMiningAddr(0x139bd2ec) (0x82890cc1, block 73928353, 2026-01-03; lpMiningAddr in slot 0xf), 49 blocks after the token's deployment (0x60ee522a): it granted the LP-mining contract the extractFromPoolForLpMining power that burns the deferred amount from the pair (rule 8). The owner's excludeMultipleAccountsFromFee (0x2ede033c, block 84454484, 2026-03-03) set _isExcludedFromFee for the router (slot 0x8c3bf988) and the pair (0x8e214e2e), so pair-to-router swaps bypass the deflation-phase buy ban, which is how the flash-funded attacker obtained the 20M MT it sold. Like setPresale (0xdcc40744, block 84470962, the launch switch), it lifts a trading restriction as a pause does and is not a reset (rule 8), and a holder with enough MT could have run the deferred burn without it; counting it would give an age of 6.4 days.

The LP-mining contracts 0x139bd2ec (lpMiningAddr, whose distributeDailyRewards called extractFromPoolForLpMining) and 0x048f012b (fee processor) are unverified and not listed: the burn from the pair is MT's _executePendingBurn. lastPoolExtractionTime allows one extraction per UTC day, and the day's extraction had not yet run when the attacker triggered it.

Earlier exploits: campaign.mjs --outflows over the pair's WBNB from the deployment finds only 0.19 WBNB (0x3cc54920, an LP removal) and dust before the anchor; the later outflows (0x3e8d5c0f, 0xcfa663db and smaller) are LP removals and the deployer's sells into the drained pair.

Loss is the pair's net WBNB outflow in the anchor (1,595.95 out against 1,214.21 the attacker paid in), equal to the 381.75 WBNB sent to the attacker EOA 0xdb0901a3; the MT burned from or left in the pair is unpriced and not counted.
